questions.question_english: Consider the two statements below: Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Assertion (A): A son suffering from severe permanent physical disability is eligible for dependent medical benefits even after crossing the age of 25 years. Reason (R): The rules mandate that dependent status for disabled children continues irrespective of age, provided the disability occurred before attaining the age of 25 years and they remain financially dependent.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of. A Statutory health provisions make an exception to the standard age limit of twenty-five years for sons suffering from permanent physical or mental disabilities. If the disability manifested prior to reaching age twenty-five and renders the child incapable of self-support, dependent status continues indefinitely, validating the continuation of full medical benefits.

questions.question_english: Consider the following statements regarding the CGHS card: I. It contains a unique beneficiary identification number. II. It is strictly non-transferable. III. Misuse of the card can lead to penal action and withdrawal of facilities. IV. It is valid only in the specific city where it was issued. Which of the statements given above are correct?

अभिकथन (A): CGHS के दायरे में दंत-उपचार पूरी तरह शामिल नहीं है।
कारण (R): सरकारी स्वास्थ्य योजनाओं में दंत समस्याओं को चिकित्सा समस्या के बजाय सौंदर्य-संबंधी माना जाता है। सही संबंध चुनिए।
options_hindi: A और R दोनों सही हैं, और R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता
A सही है, लेकिन R गलत है
A गलत है, लेकिन R सही है
questions.question_english: Consider the two statements below: Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Assertion (A): Dental treatment is entirely excluded from the purview of CGHS. Reason (R): Dental issues are considered cosmetic rather than medical under government health schemes.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: A is false but R is true. Dental treatment is not excluded from health scheme provisions; outpatient dental consultations, tooth extractions, root canal treatments, and routine dental procedures are fully covered at government dental units or empanelled centers. Purely cosmetic dental enhancements are excluded, but comprehensive dental care remains an integral component of scheme benefits.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। A गलत है, लेकिन R सही है। स्रोत में दिए गए कथन और संबंधित नियमों के आधार पर यही संबंध सही है।
key_facts: Answer key: (D)

questions.question_english: Under the provisions of the PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal) scheme, if a child falls ill after consuming school food, what is the immediate responsibility of the School Principal regarding medical attendance?
options_english: Contact the parents immediately and instruct them to bear medical costs under CS(MA) rules
Keep the child resting in school and wait for the local CMO I/C to visit the premises
Issue an administrative suspension order for the child until health clearance is produced
Transport the child immediately to the nearest hospital/health centre for emergency care
questions.explanation_english: Transport the child immediately to the nearest hospital/health centre for emergency care. Student health and safety mandate immediate emergency intervention during school health crises, such as suspected food poisoning under school meal programs. The School Principal must immediately arrange transport for affected students to the nearest public hospital or healthcare facility for urgent medical evaluation, prioritizing child welfare over administrative paperwork.

questions.question_english: A retired Principal moves to a rural village where no CGHS wellness centre exists within a 100 km radius. She wishes to undergo an elective hernia surgery. What is the most procedurally correct method for her to utilize her CGHS pensioner card?
options_english: Admit herself to the local rural clinic and submit actual medical bills for reimbursement
Visit a CGHS wellness centre for a CMO I/C referral to an empanelled hospital
Demand cashless surgical facilities directly from the local un-empanelled private clinic
Forfeit her surgical treatment entitlement since her residence lies outside CGHS coverage
questions.explanation_english: Visit a CGHS wellness centre for a CMO I/C referral to an empanelled hospital. A pensioner holding a valid scheme card seeking elective surgery must follow standard procedural guidelines. Even if residing away from a wellness centre, elective non-emergency surgery requires visiting a scheme wellness centre to secure a formal referral to an empanelled hospital for cashless treatment or approved reimbursement.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है: CGHS वेलनेस केंद्र जाकर CMO I/C से सूचीबद्ध अस्पताल के लिए रेफरल लेना। स्रोत में दिए गए स्पष्टीकरण के अनुसार यही नियम, पात्रता-शर्त या प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया इस प्रश्न पर लागू होती है।

The employee must be a Gazetted Officer.
The employee must be residing in a CGHS covered area.

The chief vigilance officer of the affiliated government hospital
The Mayor of the local municipal corporation and local councillors

The government reimburses the full actual billed amount as an exceptional administrative case
The empanelled hospital is penalized for admitting the employee above their entitled ward class
Reimbursement is capped at entitlement rates, and the employee pays room rent differences

Obtaining a valid referral from a CGHS Wellness Centre or a Government Specialist

questions.explanation_english: Obtaining a valid referral from a CGHS Wellness Centre or a Government Specialist. No, travelling expenses for an accompanying attendant are strictly non-reimbursable by law

Acupuncture performed by private non- medical practitioners

questions.explanation_english: Acupuncture performed by private non- medical practitioners.
